## Introduction & Market Context
Mastercard Incorporated (NYSE:MA) presented its third-quarter 2026 financial results on October 29, 2026, revealing stronger-than-expected performance that sent shares surging near their 52-week high. The payment network giant reported adjusted earnings of $5.31 per share on revenue of $9.8 billion, topping Wall Street estimates of $5.16 and $9.65 billion, respectively.

Net revenue climbed 14% year-over-year to $9.8 billion on both an as-adjusted and currency-neutral basis. Adjusted operating income increased 15% to $5.9 billion, while the adjusted operating margin expanded 70 basis points to 60.5%. The company’s adjusted net income rose 17% on an as-adjusted basis and 18% on a currency-neutral basis, reaching $4.7 billion.

[Mastercard](https://www.geminiq.com/stocks/MA)'s Q3 2026 operating cash flow was $5.09 billion, down 10.2% from $5.66 billion a year earlier, while net income rose 17.9%. The release led with 14% revenue growth and called the quarter strong; the cash flow statement carries the gap.  
**The Data:** Over nine months, operating cash flow was **$11.86 billion**, down $787 million from $12.65 billion, while net income rose 18% to $12.90 billion. That puts operating cash at about 92% of net income, against about 116% a year earlier. Payment network rebates and incentives reached $6.37 billion in Q3, up 18% against payment network revenue growth of 11%.
The disconfirming evidence is in the sequence: Q3 operating cash flow rose 34.8% from Q2's $3.77 billion, and at about 110% of net income it was still the third highest of the last 16 quarters. The year-ago quarter, at about 144% of net income, set an unusually high bar.
Mastercard's Q3 2026 free cash flow, operating cash flow less capital expenditure, was $4.87 billion, down 11.3% from $5.49 billion a year earlier. Capital expenditure rose 24.7% to $222 million, so roughly 7% of the $0.62 billion decline traces to higher spending and the rest to operating cash.
